description: Mercimek Corbasi is a beloved Turkish Red Lentil Soup, a staple in every Turkish home. This comforting and hearty soup is known for its smooth texture and rich, savory flavor, often enhanced with a tangy lemon squeeze. It is incredibly nutritious, easy to prepare, and perfect for any meal of the day, offering warmth and satisfaction in every spoonful.

instructions.title: Prepare Lentils and Aromatics
instructions.text: Thoroughly rinse the red lentils under cold water until the water runs clear; drain well. In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat the olive oil and 1 tablespoon of butter over medium heat. Add the chopped onion and sauté for 5 minutes until softened and translucent.

instructions.title: Build the Flavor Base
instructions.text: Add the minced garlic to the pot and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. Sprinkle in the all-purpose flour and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring to create a roux.

instructions.title: Combine with Liquid and Lentils
instructions.text: Gradually whisk in the chicken or vegetable broth and water, ensuring no lumps form. Add the rinsed and drained red lentils, salt, and black pepper to the pot. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low.

instructions.title: Simmer to Perfection
instructions.text: Cover the pot and let the soup simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until the lentils are completely tender and have broken down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking to the bottom of the pot.

instructions.title: Blend the Soup
instructions.text: Remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is smooth and creamy. Alternatively, you can transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender and blend until smooth, then return it to the pot.

instructions.title: Prepare Spiced Butter Topping
instructions.text: In a small pan, melt the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter over medium-low heat. Add the dried mint and red pepper flakes (pul biber) and cook for 30 seconds, just until fragrant, being careful not to burn the spices. This creates the traditional Turkish topping.

instructions.title: Serve Mercimek Corbasi
instructions.text: Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into individual bowls. Drizzle a spoonful of the spiced butter topping over each serving. Garnish with fresh chopped mint or parsley, and serve immediately with a lemon wedge on the side for squeezing.

tips: For an extra authentic touch, ensure your soup is blended until perfectly smooth. This creamy texture is characteristic of traditional Mercimek Corbasi. An immersion blender makes this step quick and easy.
Use good quality Turkish red pepper flakes (pul biber) and dried mint for the butter topping. These spices are key to the soup's distinctive aroma and flavor, adding a vibrant finish.
Always serve Mercimek Corbasi piping hot with a fresh lemon wedge. A squeeze of lemon juice brightens the soup's flavor and cuts through the richness, elevating the entire dish.
article:
Mercimek Corbasi: The Soul-Soothing Turkish Red Lentil Soup

In the heart of Turkish cuisine lies a warmth that transcends mere flavor – it’s a feeling, a comfort, a hug in a bowl. Among the many culinary treasures, one dish stands out for its humble ingredients and extraordinary taste: Mercimek Corbasi, or Turkish Red Lentil Soup. This vibrant, creamy, and utterly delicious soup is a staple in every Turkish home, restaurant, and even street vendor’s cart. From bustling cityscapes to serene village kitchens, the aroma of simmering red lentils, fragrant mint, and sizzling butter is a universally recognized call to comfort. It’s a dish that embodies the very spirit of hospitality and home, offering nourishment and joy in every spoonful. Whether you’re seeking a light lunch, a comforting dinner starter, or a restorative meal, Mercimek Corbasi is a culinary embrace you won't soon forget.

## What is Mercimek Corbasi Red Lentil Soup?

Mercimek Corbasi translates directly to "lentil soup," but it’s specifically made with red lentils, giving it its characteristic orange-red hue and smooth, creamy texture. Unlike some lentil soups that are chunky and hearty, Mercimek Corbasi is traditionally pureed to a silky consistency, making it incredibly comforting and easy to digest. Its roots are deeply embedded in Anatolian culinary traditions, where lentils have been a primary food source for centuries due due to their affordability, nutritional value, and versatility.

This beloved soup is more than just food; it’s a cultural icon. It’s often the first thing offered to guests, a go-to remedy for colds, and a perfect starter for any meal, from a simple family dinner to a grand celebratory feast. The flavor profile is a delicate balance of savory, slightly tangy, and wonderfully aromatic. A base of sautéed onions and garlic, often enriched with a touch of tomato paste, forms the foundation. The magic truly happens with the addition of dried mint and red pepper flakes, which are typically infused into a sizzling butter or olive oil drizzle just before serving. This final flourish adds a burst of freshness, a subtle heat, and a beautiful visual appeal. The result is a profoundly satisfying and wholesome Turkish Red Lentil Soup that appeals to all ages and palates. It’s naturally gluten-free (if no flour is used) and can easily be made vegan, making it a universally appreciated dish.

## Ingredients You Need

Creating an authentic Turkish Red Lentil Soup requires a few simple, readily available ingredients. The beauty of Mercimek Corbasi lies in how these humble components transform into something truly extraordinary.

*   **Red Lentils:** About 1 cup. These cook quickly and break down easily, giving the soup its signature creamy texture. Ensure they are well rinsed.
*   **Onion:** 1 medium, finely chopped. Provides a sweet and aromatic base.
*   **Garlic:** 2-3 cloves, minced. Adds depth of flavor.
*   **Tomato Paste:** 1-2 tablespoons. Adds a rich umami depth and a subtle tanginess, enhancing the soup's color.
*   **Flour (optional):** 1 tablespoon. A common addition for slight thickening, though many recipes achieve thickness purely through blending.
*   **Olive Oil or Butter:** 2 tablespoons for sautéing, plus additional for the garnish. Olive oil is traditional for the soup base, butter is key for the finishing drizzle.
*   **Water or Vegetable/Chicken Broth:** 6-7 cups. Broth adds more flavor, but water is perfectly acceptable and traditional for a lighter taste.
*   **Salt & Black Pepper:** To taste. Essential for seasoning.
*   **Dried Mint (Nane):** 1-2 teaspoons for the garnish. This is a crucial flavor component; don't skip it!
*   **Red Pepper Flakes (Pul Biber or Aleppo Pepper):** 1-2 teaspoons for the garnish. Adds a mild, fruity heat and vibrant color. Adjust to your spice preference.
*   **Lemon Wedges:** For serving. A squeeze of fresh lemon juice is non-negotiable for authentic flavor.

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Making Mercimek Corbasi is a straightforward process, perfect for cooks of all skill levels. Follow these steps for a perfect bowl of Turkish Red Lentil Soup every time:

1.  **Prepare the Lentils:** Rinse 1 cup of red lentils thoroughly under cold running water until the water runs clear. This removes any starch and debris. Set aside.
2.  **Sauté Aromatics:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil or butter over medium heat. Add the finely chopped onion and sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, but not browned. Add the minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
3.  **Add Tomato Paste and Flour (if using):** Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, to deepen its flavor. If using flour, sprinkle it over the mixture and cook for another minute, stirring to combine and cook out the raw flour taste.
4.  **Combine with Lentils and Liquid:** Add the rinsed red lentils to the pot. Pour in 6-7 cups of water or broth. Add salt and black pepper to taste. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until the lentils are very tender and have started to break down. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
5.  **Blend Until Smooth:** Once the lentils are cooked, remove the pot from the heat. Using an immersion blender, carefully blend the soup directly in the pot until it is completely smooth and creamy, with no discernible lentil pieces. Alternatively, transfer the soup in batches to a regular blender (be cautious with hot liquids – fill only halfway, vent the lid, and cover with a towel) and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
6.  **Adjust Consistency and Seasoning:** If the soup is too thick, add a little more hot water or broth until it reaches your desired consistency. Taste and adjust salt and pepper if needed. Keep warm over very low heat.
7.  **Prepare the Garnish (Nane-Pul Biberli Yağ):** In a small saucepan or skillet, melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium-low heat. Once the butter is melted and slightly foamy, remove it from the heat. Stir in 1-2 teaspoons of dried mint and 1-2 teaspoons of red pepper flakes. The residual heat will infuse the flavors into the butter.
8.  **Serve:** Ladle the hot Mercimek Corbasi into bowls. Drizzle each serving generously with the prepared mint and red pepper flake butter. Serve immediately with fresh lemon wedges on the side for squeezing.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving that perfect, authentic Mercimek Corbasi is all about attention to detail. These pro tips will elevate your Turkish Red Lentil Soup from good to unforgettable:

*   **Rinse Those Lentils:** Don't skip rinsing! It removes excess starch, which can make the soup cloudy and sometimes affect the texture. A thorough rinse ensures a cleaner, brighter flavor.
*   **Sautéing is Key:** Take your time sautéing the onions and garlic. Developing their sweetness and aroma is the foundation of the soup's flavor. Don't let them brown, just soften.
*   **Cook the Tomato Paste:** Cooking the tomato paste for a minute or two before adding liquids caramelizes its sugars, deepening its flavor and reducing any raw metallic taste. This step is crucial for a rich, well-rounded soup.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** The signature texture of Mercimek Corbasi is its velvety smoothness. Blend thoroughly until there are absolutely no chunks left. An immersion blender makes this process incredibly easy.
*   **The Power of the Drizzle:** The mint and red pepper flake butter drizzle is not just a garnish; it's an integral part of the flavor profile. The sizzling butter awakens the aromatics of the dried mint and the gentle heat of the pul biber, adding a final layer of complexity and freshness that truly defines this Turkish Red Lentil Soup.
*   **Don't Forget the Lemon:** A squeeze of fresh lemon juice just before eating is non-negotiable. It brightens the soup, balances the richness, and adds a zesty tang that cuts through the creaminess. Always serve with lemon wedges on the side.
*   **Let It Rest:** If time permits, let the soup sit for 10-15 minutes after blending and before serving. This allows the flavors to meld further and the soup to settle into its perfect consistency.

## Serving Suggestions

Mercimek Corbasi is incredibly versatile and can be enjoyed in many ways, depending on the meal and your preference.

*   **With a Squeeze of Lemon:** As mentioned, a generous squeeze of fresh lemon juice is essential. It brightens the flavors and adds a tangy counterpoint to the rich lentils.
*   **The Chili-Mint Butter:** Always serve with the traditional drizzle of butter infused with dried mint and red pepper flakes. This adds a beautiful aroma, a subtle kick, and a vibrant color.
*   **Crusty Bread:** A warm, crusty piece of Turkish bread (like pide), a slice of sourdough, or even just some good quality white bread for dipping is the perfect accompaniment.
*   **Pickles (Turşu):** In Turkey, it's common to serve soups with a side of mixed pickles. Their sour crunch provides a wonderful contrast to the creamy soup.
*   **As a Starter:** Mercimek Corbasi makes an excellent appetizer for any meal, from a light lunch to a more elaborate dinner featuring grilled meats or other Turkish dishes.
*   **Light Meal:** Paired with a simple salad, this nourishing soup can easily stand on its own as a fulfilling and healthy light meal.
*   **Garnish Variations:** While the butter drizzle is classic, you can also sprinkle with a pinch of sumac for extra tang, a dash of extra pul biber for more heat, or a few sprigs of fresh parsley or cilantro for color and freshness.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Turkish Red Lentil Soup is perfect as is, there are several ways to adapt it to your taste or dietary needs.

*   **Add Vegetables:** For a heartier soup, you can add finely diced carrots or potatoes along with the lentils. These will cook down and blend seamlessly into the soup, adding extra nutrients and a subtle sweetness. Add them after sautéing the aromatics and before the liquid.
*   **Different Broths:** While water is traditional, using vegetable or chicken broth will add more depth of flavor. Ensure vegetable broth is unsalted if you're sensitive to sodium.
*   **Spice It Up (or Down):** Adjust the amount of red pepper flakes (pul biber) in the butter drizzle to suit your heat preference. For a spicier kick, you can also add a pinch of cayenne pepper to the soup itself while simmering. For milder versions, reduce or omit the pul biber.
*   **Vegan Option:** To make this soup completely vegan, simply use vegetable broth instead of chicken broth and olive oil instead of butter for both the sautéing and the final drizzle. The flavor will still be incredibly robust and satisfying.
*   **Other Spices:** While not strictly traditional, some variations might include a pinch of cumin or turmeric for an earthy undertone. Add these with the tomato paste to toast their flavors.
*   **Thickening Alternatives:** If you prefer not to use flour, you can simply rely on the natural starch of the lentils and the blending process to achieve thickness. Cooking the lentils longer until they are very soft will also contribute to a thicker consistency.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** For a subtle smoky note, you can use smoked paprika in the butter drizzle alongside the pul biber.

Mercimek Corbasi is more than just a recipe; it's an invitation to experience a piece of Turkish culture and hospitality. Its comforting warmth and vibrant flavors make it a beloved dish across the globe. So gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to embark on a culinary journey to the heart of Anatolia with every spoonful of this exquisite Turkish Red Lentil Soup. Afiyet olsun! (Bon appétit!)
